macro.regime: Hawkish-hike repricing, AI-leadership shock absorbed by a Nvidia beat
macro.narrative: The two-day Mon-Tue selloff (S&P -1.92% then -1.03% to 7340.53; VIX 19.30 -> 22.91 -> 25.46) is primarily a Fed-repricing shock, not a growth scare: CME-style odds for the Dec 9 FOMC have hardened further to roughly 95-98% for a 25bp HIKE (from ~75-89% a day earlier), with St. Louis Fed's Musalem floating four hikes into spring 2027 and Waller open to 50bp on an inflation surprise, while NY Fed's Williams ruled out only the size of a jumbo move, not the direction. Layered on top is a chip-sector-specific unwind: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's Nov 12 resignation (an affair with a woman US officials were probing as a possible Chinese-intelligence-linked contact; Colette Kress now interim CEO) created leadership uncertainty into Tuesday's Q3 FY27 report -- which beat big (revenue $115.8B vs $109.1B est., Q4 guide ~$130B vs $125.3B est.) and rose after hours, even as chip peers (Micron, Intel, Marvell, Arm, AMD, Broadcom) were sold off -4% to -7.6% ahead of the print on AI-capex-sustainability doubts. Credit is confirming only at the margin: HY OAS ~334bp, up from cycle lows but below the 10yr average (~383bp); real stress is concentrated in CCC-and-below (~1,300bp, 99th percentile), i.e. idiosyncratic weak-credit stress, not a systemic blowout. October retail sales (control group +0.6% vs +0.4% est.) showed resilient consumer demand, reinforcing the hawkish case rather than offsetting it. A notable decoupling Tuesday: gold/silver held up (gold ~flat, SLV +0.59%, miners GDX/SLVP/SILJ/HL all firmer) even as DXY stayed near 20-month highs, while the rare-earth basket (MP -3.41%, Lynas -8.24%) sold off into the 18-19 Nov Trump-Xi-Putin Shenzhen trilateral despite the underlying China-controls-rare-earths thesis arguably strengthening (export-control suspension extended to 10 Jan 2027; MP's 100% DoD magnet offtake and $110/kg NdPr price floor). New US Commerce rules (16-17 Nov) closed the AI-chip 'remote access' loophole and extended licensing to Singapore/Malaysia/Indonesia/Thailand/Brazil, triggering Tuesday's HK-tech divergence (Tencent -3.69%, SMIC +6.77% on a domestic-foundry rotation, Xiaomi +2.13%).
